15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable white-background game featuring a floating cup pouring water into a cartoon target representing a butt crack.
- Change gameplay so the cup moves horizontally and pours only after tapping the cup or an on-screen button.

## Requirements
- The cup must move back and forth across the screen.
- Tapping the cup must trigger it to pour.
- Tapping at the correct horizontal position must land water in the target.
- Keep the experience playable on mobile and desktop.

## Decisions
- The target is represented as a friendly peach-shaped character with a visible central crack and blue shorts waistband.
- A fixed-angle, timed pour was introduced so taps trigger a 58° tilt instead of using a manual slider.
- A mobile-friendly “POUR” button and pointer/touch cup detection were added.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` as a complete canvas-based game.
- Added a white background, floating cup, cartoon target, water particles, win state, reset control, HUD, and responsive layout.
- Added touch/pointer and keyboard support for the pour action.
- Added the moving-cup UI structure and replaced the tilt slider with a “POUR” control.

### Active
- Completing the new moving-cup gameplay integration.
- Updating cup geometry and water spawning to use the dynamically moving horizontal position.
- Removing or avoiding remaining references to the old slider-based tilt implementation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `geometry()` to calculate `cupX` from the moving `cupX` state with clamped bounds.
2. Make the cup move continuously left/right in `draw()`.
3. Spawn and tilt water only while `pourTime > 0`, decrementing it over real time.
4. Make missed pours stop contributing to the target score.
5. Test tapping/clicking the moving cup and the POUR button in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main and only game implementation; partially updated for tap-driven, moving gameplay.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build on the playable cup-pouring game with endless rounds and increasing difficulty.
- Make the cup speed up through level 10, then make the target move up to level 10; add slope obstacles that water must navigate.

## Requirements
- Cup speed increases once every 5 rounds, capped at level 10.
- After the cup reaches level 10, target movement increases once every 5 rounds, capped at level 10.
- Add slope obstacles that affect the water’s path.
- Keep the existing tap-to-pour game playable on mobile and desktop.

## Decisions
- The target is a friendly cartoon character with a visible central seam and blue waistband.
- Pouring is triggered by tapping the cup, the POUR button, or Space; the pour is a short burst.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a canvas-based game in `index.html` with a moving cup, target, water particles, HUD, reset control, and responsive layout.
- Added moving-cup gameplay, timed pouring, and hit detection for taps on the cup.
- Updated the subtitle to “An endless timing challenge” and added round and level HUD elements.

### Active
- Implement endless-round progression and reset pour/cup state between rounds.
- Implement cup and target levels, with the requested five-round progression and level caps.
- Add slope obstacles and water collision/deflection.
- Verify the updated game in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` and finish the round progression; current win handling only sets `won` and shows the win toast.
2. Add and render slope obstacles, then handle water collisions so slopes redirect or block drops.
3. Test round progression, level caps, obstacle behavior, and mobile/desktop input.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main and only game implementation; partial endless-game changes are in progress.

## Important Context
- Current code tracks `caught`, `won`, `cupX`, `pourTime`, and `cooldown`; `won` currently disables further pours.
- The most recent edits added `id="levels"` and `id="round"` elements, but the HUD update and game progression do not yet use them.
- A JavaScript syntax check and `git diff --check` passed before the latest HUD edits; no browser test has been done.

- The cup speeds up one level every five rounds, capped at level 10.
- Once the cup reaches level 10, the target starts moving; its movement level then increases every five rounds, also capped at 10.
- Filling the target clears the round and starts the next one automatically. Reset returns to round 1.
